subject: Service continuity carveout for single-region edge cluster — Aurora Analytics
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout for multi-region failover (APAC edge)

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. We're excited to onboard Redwood for our real-time inference layer. One blocker from our side: our primary deployment for a subservice runs in a third-party APAC edge provider that does not replicate to another region — it's a compliance requirement for a local partner.

Because of that, Aurora needs clarity on how Redwood will support an SLA for multi-region failover. We understand Redwood's standard multi-region RTO target is <1 hour, but in our architecture full state replication isn't possible immediately. Can we request a temporary carveout that documents higher RTO/RPO for the apac-edge cluster while we implement a warm-standby plan?

Specifically, we're asking for:
- A documented exception in the contract for the apac-edge cluster for 6 months with RTO up to 6 hours and RPO up to 1 hour,
- Mandatory quarterly failover drills to validate the runbook, and
- Clear monitoring and notification thresholds during the carveout period.

I've attached our SOC2 checklist and a draft runbook that shows current limitations. Happy to jump on a call this afternoon.

Best,
Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Ops, Aurora Analytics
attachments: Aurora-SOC2-Checklist-2026.pdf, aurora-mitigation-runbook-v1.md

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for multi-region failover (APAC edge)

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the artifacts. Appreciate the constraints with your APAC edge partner.

High-level response and next steps:
1) We can consider a timeboxed SLA carveout for the apac-edge cluster, contingent on a mutually agreed runbook, scheduled failover drills, and additional telemetry.
2) For contract language we'll need: explicit RTO/RPO numbers, a fixed review cadence (we usually do 90 days), a remediation plan if drills fail, and an acceptance criteria definition for a successful drill.
3) Marcus (SRE) will review the runbook and propose the operational mitigations and cost impacts (dedicated warm resources, cache-warming strategies).

Would you be able to share a preferred 2-hour window next week for a technical deep dive? After that meeting, we'll draft the exception addendum and route for legal/finance review.

Copied Laura because this impacts contractual language and approval thresholds above my signing authority.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for multi-region failover (APAC edge)

Thanks Samir — I went through the draft runbook. Two quick notes from an SRE perspective:

1) Realistic recovery profile if we do a conditional carveout:
   - Customer data: if not replicated, RPO realistically equals the last successful object sync. For your current pipeline that looks like ~up to 60 minutes under normal conditions.
   - Service recovery (control plane + model serving): cold-starting containers and rebuilding KV caches will add significant time. With a cold standby we estimate 2–4 hours to reach functional latency (95th percentile), and an additional 1–2 hours to warm the KV cache to pre-failure tail latencies.

2) Mitigations to meet the ask (RTO <= 6h, RPO <= 1h):
   - Implement a small warm pool in a proximate region (paid reserved capacity) to allow faster container spin-up and partial KV cache snapshots.
   - Use prefix/KV cache checkpointing to disk and a prioritized pre-warm sequence (models -> critical prefixes).
   - Nightly incremental snapshot pushes from apac-edge to a secure staging bucket in ap-southeast-1 (encrypted at rest).

3) Operational requirements and acceptance criteria for drills:
   - Successful failover in <6h from notification, with validation queries demonstrating <2x production latency for critical paths.
   - Drill runbook run and post-mortem within 72 hours.

4) Cost and billing: warm pool and snapshot replication will be billable to the customer as a Dedicated Add-on during the carveout period. We'll include a cost estimate in the next note.

If Aurora agrees to those mitigations and pay the warm-pool add-on, we can propose the draft exception language. Suggest a 6-month carveout with a mandatory failover drill at month 3 and month 6.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments referenced: aurora-mitigation-runbook-v1.md

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for multi-region failover (APAC edge)

Samir — thank you for the thorough context and for working with Marcus on the operational plan. I’ve reviewed the proposed mitigations.

Decision (conditional approval):
We will approve a timeboxed carveout for Aurora Analytics specific to the named apac-edge cluster under the following conditions:

1) Duration: 6 months from the effective date in the addendum.
2) SLA during carveout: RTO up to 6 hours, RPO up to 1 hour. This exception will be explicitly scoped to the apac-edge cluster and will not apply to other accounts or regions.
3) Operational commitments from Aurora: provide write access to nightly snapshot targets, participate in a full failover drill at months 3 and 6, and complete an agreed post-drill remediation plan if acceptance criteria are not met.
4) Redwood commitments: provide a warm-pool plan (capacity and cost estimate), runbooks, and 24x7 on-call coverage during drills. Redwood will also deliver a drill report and a remediation plan within 72 hours of any failed drill.
4) Billing: warm-pool capacity and cross-region snapshot storage will be billed as a Dedicated Add-on per the attached estimate.

Next steps: Sean will prepare the exception addendum and share it with Aurora and our legal team. Finance will attach a cost estimate for the warm pool. Marcus will schedule a technical review and provide the initial cost numbers by EOD Thursday.

If that aligns with Aurora, Sean: please coordinate with Samir on scheduling the technical deep dive next week.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
